content.title: Reply to Reviewer #2 - Part 2
content.comment:
5. > Like previous method, it is important to validate the proposed method under longer training epochs, such as 300 epochs. Could you provide these experiments?

What do you mean by "a longer training epochs"? Pre-training epochs or fine-tuning epochs?

* If you say pretraining epochs, previous methods, i.e., UP-DETR and DETReg, do not provide the results of pretraining for a longer epochs, like 300 epochs. Their pre-training scheme is similar to us, i.e., pre-training for 60 epochs.

  One reason why previous works, i.e., UP-DETR and DETReg, only pre-train the DETR for 60 epochs (compared to 400 or more epochs in conventional SSL) might be previous works all use a SwAV backbone to initialize their CNN backbone, therefore 60 epochs for Transformer might be enough. We will add 400 epochs or longer experiments in the future.

* If you say fine-tuning epochs, we think longer fine-tuning scheme deviates from the intention of pre-training. Our goal is the pre-trained models can converges fast on downstream datasets. And our Siamese DETR with 150 epochs can achieve competitive results compared to UP-DETR with 300 epochs (42.0 mAP vs. 42.8 mAP).

6. > Type error: In section 4.3, the main text shows UP-DETR performs 56.9 mAP on PASCAL VOC, but the number is 56.7 in the Table 3.

Thank for you advice. We modify this type error in rebuttal version.

content.title: Reply to Reviewer #2 - Part 1
content.comment:
1. > Although the proposed method is a new multi-view pretraining approach, the novelty in the proposed method is not enough. Compared with previous methods, the proposed method utilizes multi-view learning. But, the multi-view learning is a common technique in contrastive learning. From this perspective, it is incremental. 

The novelty of Siamese DETR is not simply an improvement over previous methods (i.e., UP-DETR) using multi-view learning techniques.

Specifically, we introduce siamese network in the design of the pre-training pipeline. Through combining the characterisitics of cross-attenion with the siamese network, Siamese DETR can aggregate the information of key view given the cue of query view, and then detect the corresponding regions. This is completely different with the common multi-view learning techniques, i.e., simply contrasting the output of DETR given the input of two augmented view. To my best knowledge, it is the first paper to combine siamese network with DETR.

The proposed cross-view cross-attention mechanism enables the model to learn the view-invariant localization ability, which is completely different from the previous method (i.e., UP-DETR) that only detects the background in most of pre-training time. Furthermore, we also use offline object proposals to introduce objectness priors to provide better candidate regions.

2. > In addition, the training cost (e.g. GPU Mem) is higher than previous methods, such as UP-DETR and DETReg. 

Siamese DETR does not require huge memory compared to UP-DETR and DETReg, because all parameters in the siamese network are shared. We compare the GPU memory cost and iteration time among the three methods using Conditional DETR on COCO. Given the input of the same batch size and the same size augmentation on the same GPU, we calculate the average GPU memory cost and iteration time using 1000 stable iterations.

\* Notice that Siamese DETR and UP-DETR are implemented using MMSelfSup, and DETReg is implemented using its released repository. Several hooks used in MMSelfSup may slow down the iteration time, therefore the iteration time of DETReg is for reference only.
|Method|GPU Mem.|Iteration time|
|:----:|:----:|:----:|
|Siamese DETR|8428 MB| 0.8018 s/it|
|UP-DETR|8199 MB| 0.7524 s/it|
|DETReg*|10528 MB|0.5028 s/it|

DETReg requires most GPU memory because it also maintains an extra SwAV model except DETR. For iteration time, the increase time of Siamese DETR compared to UP-DETR is slight. 

3. > In the section 4.1 Finetuning, the authors use 64 as the batch size for their method. To my knowledge, UP-DETR and DETRReg set the batch size to 32. The batch size can affect the detection performance. Therefore, it is unfair to conduct comparison under different batch size settings. Could you give more experiments about it?

We use a batch size of 64 when fintuning Vanilla DETR follow the origin setting in DETR paper. For a fair comparison, we conduct three extra experiments using Vanilla DETR with a batch size of 32 in fine-tuning. We update the detailed results in the rebuttal version.  (The rebuttal version will update tomorrow) We also provide abbreviated results below.

|Dataset|Batch size|mAP|
|:----:|:----:|:----:|
|ImageNet->COCO@epoch150|64|42.0|
|ImageNet->COCO@eopch150|32|42.0|
|ImageNet->VOC@epoch50|64|53.6|
|ImageNet->VOC@epoch50|32|54.4|
|ImageNet->VOC@epoch150|64|57.0|
|ImageNet->VOC@epoch150|32|57.4|

In ImageNet -> COCO setup, the change in performance is very slight. And in ImageNet -> VOC setup, using a small batch size improves the results. It is because a smaller batch size leads to more optimization steps. Considering the PASCAL VOC is relatively small, the model with smaller batch size converges better.

4. > In Table 1, Table 2, and Table 4, the detection performance of DETReg only exists in a few settings. Could you complete the missing comparison with DETReg? 

We complete part of missing results of DETReg in rebuttal version. We will complete the rest later.

content.title: Reply to Reviewer #1
content.comment:
1. > Clarity of the paper could be improved, especially section 3 and Figure 2. While the approach is understandable, I was a bit confused at first by the notation. Adding the dimensionality of the different variables could help as they sometime refer to feature map, set of vectors or flat average-pooled vector. I would also suggest using different function name for the CNN encoder, transformer encoder, decoder.

Thanks for your advice. We will add dimensionality of different variables and replace the $f(x;\theta)$ expression with $\texttt{Backbone}(x)$ in rebuttal version later.

2. > The approach is only compared to DETR variants. It’s unclear if the approach brings some benefit compared to other object detection work such as VITDet (from Exploring Plain Vision Transformer Backbones for Object Detection, Li et al. 2022).

> While the paper shows that Siamese DETR outperforms other DETR variant, it is unclear if one should use this approach compared to other recent object detection baseline. To better demonstrate the significance of Siamese DETR, I would encourage the author to compare with a broader set of object detection baselines, such as VITDet.

Siamese DETR is designed for DETR architecture, which consists of Encoder and Decoder in Transformer. The pretext tasks, especially the multi-view region detection, are specific for Decoder in Transformer. It cannot directly transfer to other object detection framework like ViTDet (has no Decoder) and traditional R-CNN pipeline.

Besides, ViTDet use MAE as initialization. We think it is difficult to directly adopt MAE-like approach on DETR architecture because the Decoder in Transformer, which aggregates the features from the output of Encoder given the condition of queries, cannot be well-pretrained.

3. > The paper only focuses on object-detection tasks. While I understand this is the focus of the current work, significance of Siamese DETR could be improved by demonstrating its applicability to other tasks such as segmentation or classificaiton.

We mainly focus on the detection pre-training, and we consider transferring Siamese DETR models to segmentation tasks in the future.

content.title: Reply to Reviewer #4
content.comment:
1. > Besides, the authors are also encouraged to verify the e!ectiveness of the proposed method based on DAB-DETR[1] and DINO-DETR[2] with various-sized backbones including R50 and Swin-L. According to their offcial implementations, DAB-Deformable-DETR-R50-v2[3] and DINO-5scale with Swin-L[4] achieve 48.7 (50epoch) and 57.3/58.0 (12epoch/36epoch) respectively.

Thanks for your advice. We verify the generalization of Siamese DETR using vanilla DETR and popular Deformable DETR. We will add DN-DETR in the experiment setting later.

Besides, results of 57.3/58.0 achieved by DINO-5scale is initialized with the model pretraining on a much huger detection dataset Object-365. And we cannot compare with it fairly. We will use DN-DETR instead.

2. > The authors should justify why the proposed method can learn better initializations for the transformer encoder and decoder considering the original Deformable DETR already explicitly encodes multiple strong priors such as locality and multi-scale. 

The designed pretext task can learn detection-oriented and view-invariant reperesentation during pretraining, thus providing a better prior in initialization. All emperical results and visualization can demonstrate it. Especially, see Table 5 in Appendix, Siamese DETR provides better AR@10 during initialization.

AR@10 during initialization:
|UP-DETR|random|Siamese DETR|
|:----:|:----:|:----:|
|17.9|0.1|23.0|

Besides, the prior learned by Deformable DETR during supervised training does not conflict with the initialization provided by Siamese DETR.

3. > Why performing the multi-view pre-training on ImageNet can help the transformer performance on the non-object centric datasets like COCO.

We introduce objectness prior, e.g., Edgeboxes or Selective Search, in ImageNet pre-training, which provides instance-level or region-level information. The capability of locating and discriminating regions in ImageNet can benefit performance in downstream datasets like COCO. We also point out Siamese DETR pre-trained on scene-centric datasets, like COCO, can achieve more significant improvements.

4. > The training settings for pretraining on ImageNet for only 5x epochs seem VERY STRANGE considering the conventional self-supervised methods such as MoCo, SimCLR, and MAE typically require more than 400 epochs. The authors should justify why although this seems to start from the previous UP-DETR, which might be not very reasonable indeed.

One reason why previous works, i.e., UP-DETR and DETReg, only pre-train the DETR for 60 epochs (compared to 400 or more epochs in conventional SSL) might be previous works all use a SwAV backbone to initialize their CNN backbone, therefore 60 epochs for Transformer might be enough. We will add 400 epochs or longer experiments in the future.

content.title: Reply to Reviewer #3
content.comment:
1. > The proposed method adopts two views in each iteration. Thus, I think that it may be not fair when comparing the proposed method with UP-DETR under the same pre-training epoch (60 epoch). Actually, the proposed model see more data (double as UP-DETR) in an epoch. It is hard to judge whether the performance gain is from the loss designs or the more data. I suggest the authors list the results of the proposed model with 30 pre-training epochs.

Multi-view training is not equivalent as training with double data. This is because:
* In MoCo or most SSL framework, only one branch (query branch) generates gradient, and another branch (key branch) adopts a "stop-gradient" strategy. Therefore, only the gradient of query branch is back-propagated, and there is no any double data usage.
* In BYOL or SimSiam, they follow "stop-gradient" strategy and further propose a symetrical loss (i.e., view1 as query and view2 as key/view1 as key and view2 as query). No one says it is unfair to compare MoCo with BYOL or SimSiam under the same epochs. It is more like a trick rather than double data usage.

Besides, We will add an extra experiment using 30 pretraining epochs later.

2. > The multi-view designs need more GPU memory and may significantly increase the pre-training time.

Siamese DETR does not require huge memory compared to UP-DETR and DETReg, because all parameters in the siamese network are shared. We compare the GPU memory cost and iteration time among the three methods using Conditional DETR on COCO. Given the input of the same batch size and the same size augmentation on the same GPU, we calculate the average GPU memory cost and iteration time using 1000 stable iterations.

\* Notice that Siamese DETR and UP-DETR are implemented using MMSelfSup, and DETReg is implemented using its released repository. Several hooks used in MMSelfSup may slow down the iteration time, therefore the iteration time of DETReg is for reference only.
|Method|GPU Mem.|Iteration time|
|:----:|:----:|:----:|
|Siamese DETR|8428 MB| 0.8018 s/it|
|UP-DETR|8199 MB| 0.7524 s/it|
|DETReg*|10528 MB|0.5028 s/it|

DETReg requires most GPU memory because it also maintains an extra SwAV model except DETR. For iteration time, the increase time of Siamese DETR compared to UP-DETR is slight.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
The paper proposes a Siamese extension of DETR for self-supervised pretraining. The main idea behind the pretraining task is 1) multi-view region detection which aims at localizing regions-of-interest between augmented views and 2) region-level discrimination.

The authors compare their approach to other DETR variants either supervised or self-supervised. Authors show some reasonable gains over those baselines on the MS-COCO and Pascal VOC dataset.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
-	To my knowledge, a Siamese extension of DETR is novel and interesting.
-	Authors empirical evaluation clearly demonstrates the benefit of their approach over other DETR variants.

Weaknesses:
-	Clarity of the paper could be improved, especially section 3 and Figure 2.  While the approach is understandable, I was a bit confused at first by the notation. Adding the dimensionality of the different variables could help as they sometime refer to feature map, set of vectors or flat average-pooled vector. I would also suggest using different function name for the CNN encoder, transformer encoder, decoder… 
-	The approach is only compared to DETR variants. It’s unclear if the approach brings some benefit compared to other object detection work such as VITDet (from Exploring Plain Vision Transformer Backbones for Object Detection, Li et al. 2022).
-	The paper only focuses on object-detection tasks. While I understand this is the focus of the current work, significance of Siamese DETR could be improved by demonstrating its applicability to other tasks such as segmentation or classificaiton.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The work seems novel to me. Quality could be improved (cf previous section), but the change  should be relatively easy to implement. It would be nice to add a reproducibility statement following ICLR recommendation.
content.summary_of_the_review:
The work proposes Siamese DETR which is a novel self-supervised extension of DETR that leverages multi-views training.  While the paper shows that Siamese DETR outperforms other DETR variant, it is unclear if one should use this approach compared to other recent object detection baseline To better demonstrate the significance of Siamese DETR, I would encourage the author to compare with a broader set of object detection baselines, such as VITDet. 

Alternatively, author could show the benefit of the pre-training scheme on other downstream tasks.

content.summary_of_the_paper: In this paper, the authors propose a new self-supervised pretraining approach for DETR. In specific, the new pretraining approach is a multi-view learning framework, which consists two self-supervised pretext tasks: multi-view region detection and multi-view semantic discrimination. Utilizing this framework, the proposed method can learn view-invariant representations with discrimination and localization.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength
+  Compared with existing method (UP-DETR and DETReg), the proposed method is a new multi-view pretraining approach and obtains better detection performance.
+ The authors provide extensive experiments to validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.
+ This paper is easily to followed and written well, especially the method section.

Weaknesses
- Although  the proposed method is a new multi-view pretraining approach, the novelty in the proposed method is not enough.  Compared with previous methods, the proposed method utilizes multi-view learning. But, the multi-view learning is a common technique in contrastive learning. From this perspective, it is incremental. In addition, the training cost (e.g. GPU Mem) is higher than  previous methods, such as  UP-DETR and DETReg. It is not practical for training with the proposed method.
- In the section 4.1 Finetuning, the authors use 64 as the batch size for their method. To my knowledge, UP-DETR and DETRReg set the batch size to 32. The batch size can affect the detection performance. Therefore, it is unfair to conduct comparison under different batch size settings. Could you give more experiments about it?
- In Table 1, Table 2, and Table 4, the detection performance of DETReg only exists in a few settings. Could you complete the missing comparison with DETReg? To my knowledge,  the code of DETReg has been published.
- Like previous method, it is important to validate the proposed method under longer training epochs, such as 300 epochs. Could you provide these experiments?
- Type error: In section 4.3, the main text shows UP-DETR performs 56.9 mAP on PASCAL VOC, but the number is 56.7 in the Table 3.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: For Clarity, Quality, Novelty, see Strength And Weaknesses. For reproducibility, it is easy to reproduce the experiments following this paper.
content.summary_of_the_review: Although  the proposed method is a new multi-view pretraining approach, the novelty in the proposed method is not enough. Meanwhile, there are some issues about the experiments, see Strength And Weaknesses. If the authors solve  all my concerns, I would raise my rate.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
This paper extends the existing single-view pretraining scheme to a multi-view pretraining scheme to perform self-supervised pre-training on the transformer modules within the DETR framework.
Specifically, the authors design two straightforward pre-text tasks including a multi-view region detection task and a multi-view semantic discrimination task.
The proposed multi-view cross-attention scheme seems reasonable and shows encouraging results across multiple DETR-based approaches including Conditional DETR and Deformable DETR.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
> Strengths

✅ The presented idea is very simple and easy to follow.

✅ The overall writing is excellent and the figures are very clear.

✅ The proposed multi-view pretraining shows encouraging results compared to the previous UP-DETR and DETReg.

> Weaknesses

❎ According to Table 1, the improvements over Deformable DETR are relatively weak and the authors should conduct experiments based on the Deformable DETR with iterative bounding box refinement and a two-stage scheme, which
already achieves 46.9 on COCO when trained with 50 epochs.
Therefore, the reported results, which only improve a WEAK baseline from 45.5 to 46.3 according to Table 1, are not convincing enough.
Besides, the authors are also encouraged to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method based on DAB-DETR[1] and DINO-DETR[2] with various-sized backbones including R50 and Swin-L.
According to their official implementations, DAB-Deformable-DETR-R50-v2[3] and DINO-5scale with Swin-L[4] achieve 48.7 (50epoch) and 57.3/58.0 (12epoch/36epoch) respectively.

[1] DAB-DETR: Dynamic Anchor Boxes are Better Queries for DETR, ICLR2022

[2] DINO: DETR with Improved DeNoising Anchor Boxes for End-to-End Object Detection, arXiv2022

[3] https://github.com/IDEA-Research/DAB-DETR#model-zoo 

[4] https://github.com/IDEA-Research/DINO#12-epoch-setting 

❎ The authors should justify why the proposed method can learn better initializations for the transformer encoder and decoder considering the original Deformable DETR already explicitly encodes multiple strong priors such as locality and multi-scale.
Why performing the multi-view pretraining on ImageNet can help the transformer performance on the non-object centric datasets like COCO.

❎ The training settings for pretraining on ImageNet for only 5x epochs seem VERY STRANGE considering the conventional self-supervised methods such as MoCo, SimCLR, and MAE typically require more than 400 epochs. The authors should justify why although
this seems to start from the previous UP-DETR, which might be not very reasonable indeed.

> Clarity

Good.

> Quality

Good.

Good.

> Reproducibility

No code is available.
content.summary_of_the_review:
How to perform pretraining that can better help the adaptation of DETR for object detection tasks is a grand challenge under strong settings and the authors' efforts are highly encouraged.
The overall idea seems novel and the results are WEAK. I will increase the ratings if the authors could well address the above-mentioned concerns.

content.title: Siamese DETR
content.abstract: Recent self-supervised methods are mainly designed for representation learning with the base model, e.g., ResNets or ViTs. They cannot be easily transferred to DETR, especially the task-specific module Transformer. In this work, we present Siamese DETR, a Siamese self-supervised pretraining approach for the Transformer architecture in DETR. We consider learning view-invariant and detection-oriented representations simultaneously through two complementary tasks, i.e., localization and discrimination, in a novel multi-view learning framework. Two self-supervised pretext tasks are designed: (a) Multi-View Region Detection aims at learning to localize regions-of-interest between augmented views of the input, and (b) Multi-View Semantic Discrimination attempts to improve object-level discrimination for each region. The proposed Siamese DETR achieves state-of-the-art transfer performance on COCO and PASCAL VOC detection using different DETR variants in all setups. Code will be made available.
